overall: Reissued on reconsideration (Chair correction only). Board violated the OML by deliberating outside a posted meeting via the April 22 email (Exhibit 11); other allegations were no violation or declined.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting about the PFAS map, including through April 22, 2021 emails.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a posted meeting via the April 22 email labeled Exhibit 11.

allegations.summary: Alleged that a March 12 virtual meeting with DEP and UMass representatives on the PFAS map was an unposted Board deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: as less than a quorum of the Board was present. Therefore, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Alleged that a Board member's April 2021 email from the shared account to the complainant (Exhibit 4) was deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Exhibit 4 did not constitute deliberation, because the email was sent from the Board’s shared email account to Mr. Hootstein, and therefore did not reach a quorum of the Board.

allegations.summary: Alleged that an April 22 email from a Board member to colleagues, criticizing the complainant (Exhibit 6), was unposted deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Although Exhibit 6 was sent by one Board member to other Board members, thus reaching a quorum, the subject of the email was not on a matter of public business within its jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board held an improper executive session on April 22 without posted notice and denied public access to the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We construe all of these allegations as alleging that the Board held an unposted “meeting” in violation of the Open Meeting Law when it engaged in email communications on April 22, and we address the allegations jointly.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board interferes in the election of future Board members.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Alleged the public was not allowed to participate in a discussion of the PFAS issue.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Additional allegations raised in the request for further review that were not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any additional allegations contained in the request for further review that were not included in the original complaints filed with the public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release the April 22 email labeled Exhibit 11 within 30 days of receipt of the determination, if not already done.
remedy_passage: We also order the Board to publicly release the email labeled Exhibit 11 within 30 days of receipt of this determination, if the Board has not already done so.
